name: Cima da Conegliano
bio: Giovanni Battista Cima, also called Cima da Conegliano, was an Italian Renaissance painter, who mostly worked in Venice. He can be considered part of the Venetian school, though he was also influenced by Antonello da Messina, in the emphasis he gives to landscape backgrounds and the tranquil atmosphere of his works.

paintings.title: Madonna of the Orange Tree
paintings.story: Madonna of the Orange Tree is a 1496–1498 oil painting on panel by Cima da Conegliano. It was originally produced for the church of Santa Chiara in Murano, from which it was confiscated for the Gallerie dell'Accademia in Venice, where it now hangs.

paintings.title: Annunciation (Cima)
paintings.story: The Annunciation is a 1495 oil on panel painting by Cima da Conegliano, now in the Hermitage Museum, in Saint Petersburg, Russia.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child (Cima, Saint Petersburg)
paintings.story: Madonna and Child is a painting in oils on canvas of 1496–1499 by Cima da Conegliano. Previously in the L. M. and K. L. Kochubey collection, it was seized by the Soviet Union's State Museum Fund and in 1921 was handed to the Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg, where it still hangs.

paintings.title: Presentation of the Virgin at the Temple (Cima)
paintings.story: The Presentation of the Virgin Mary at the Temple is a painting by the Italian Renaissance master Cima da Conegliano, c. 1496–1497, in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister of Dresden, Germany, of the Presentation of Mary. The work presents the theme, apocryphal, but common in Christian art, of the presentation of the Virgin Mary in the Temple of Jerusalem, during her childhood.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child with Saints Michael the Archangel and Andrew
paintings.story: The Madonna and Child with Saints Michael the Archangel and Andrew is an oil painting on panel by Cima da Conegliano, measuring 194x134 cm and dating to c. 1496–1498, in the Galleria nazionale di Parma.
facts: In 1706, the painting entered the Sanvital collection as a work attributed to Leonardo da Vinci owing to an apocryphal inscription in the bottom cartouche.
In 1834 it was sold to the Ducal Gallery of Parma and it was subsequently attributed to Cima da Conegliano.

paintings.title: The Archangel Raphael and Tobias with Two Saints
paintings.story: The Archangel Raphael and Tobias with Two Saints is an undated oil painting by Cima da Conegliano, now in the Gallerie dell'Accademia in Venice. To the left of the composition is Saint James the Great and to the right is Saint Nicholas of Bari. It measures 162 cm by 178 cm.

paintings.title: Dragan Altarpiece
paintings.story: Madonna and Child Enthroned with Saints is a 1496–1498 oil painting by Cima da Conegliano, originally painted on panel but later transferred to canvas. It is also known as the Dragan Altarpiece after Giorgio Dragan, a shipowner who commissioned it for his personal altar in the church of Santa Maria della Carità in Venice. To the left of the throne is a female saint, George and Nicholas, whilst to the right are Anthony Abbot, Sebastian and another female saint.

paintings.title: Saints Roch, Anthony Abbot and Lucy
paintings.story: Saints Roch, Anthony Abbot and Lucy or Three Saints is a 1513 oil on canvas painting by Cima da Conegliano, which is now in the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York.
facts: From 1843 to 1904 it was part of the Duke of Leuchtenberg’s collection at Munich and St Petersburg and was acquired by the Metropolitan Museum in 1907.
The work was once in the collection of the Empress Josephine at Malmaison (as a work of Bellini) and later in that of her son Eugène de Beauharnais, Viceroy of Italy.

paintings.title: Theseus Killing the Minotaur
paintings.story: Theseus Killing the Minotaur is an oil-on-panel painting by Cima da Conegliano, created c. 1505, now in the Museo Poldi Pezzoli in Milan. It depicts a scene of Greek mythology, when Theseus killed the Minotaur in Crete's labyrinth.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child (Cima, Paris)
paintings.story: The Madonna and Child is an oil painting on panel of 1495–1497 by the Italian Renaissance artist Cima da Conegliano, now in the Petit Palais in Paris. It was owned in London by Sir William Abdy, then in Paris by Edward Tuck, the American vice-consul there; the latter gave it to its present owner in 1930.

paintings.title: Rest on the Flight into Egypt (Cima)
paintings.story: Rest on the Flight into Egypt is a 1496–1498 oil on panel painting by Cima da Conegliano, now in the Calouste Gulbenkian Museum in Lisbon. Unusually for treatments of the scene, it also includes two saints, namely John the Baptist and Lucy.

paintings.title: Saint Peter Martyr with Saints Nicholas and Benedict
paintings.story: Saint Peter Martyr with Saints Nicholas and Benedict is an oil painting on canvas by the Italian Renaissance painter Cima da Conegliano, created c. 1505–1506, now in the Pinacoteca di Brera in Milan. It references the sacra conversazione pieces by Giovanni Bellini, whilst the landscape shows the artist as an early adopter of the new style of Giorgione.

paintings.title: Montini Altarpiece
paintings.story: The Montini Altarpiece is an oil on canvas painting by the Italian Renaissance artist Cima da Conegliano, dating from around 1506–1507 and housed in the Galleria Nazionale of Parma, Italy.

paintings.title: Christ Enthroned (Cima da Conegliano)
paintings.story: Christ Enthroned is a tempera on panel painting with gold leaf background by Cima da Conegliano, painted before 1505. Christ is seated on a marble throne, two fingers of his right hand raised in a benediction, and the left hand holding a globus cruciger. It measures 20 cm × 15 cm and was initially part of a larger altarpiece, probably its predella. It was owned by Friedrich von Pourtalès then Osip Braz, and was seized from the latter by the Soviet state on the October Revolution and assigned to the Hermitage Museum. It was transferred to the Pushkin Museum in Moscow in 1928, where it still hangs.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child (Cima, Bologna)
paintings.story: Madonna and Child is an oil-on-panel painting by the Italian Renaissance painter Cima da Conegliano, created in 1495, now in the Pinacoteca Nazionale di Bologna. A studio copy also survives in the Holburne Museum in Bath, Somerset, United Kingdom.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child (Cima, Gemona del Friuli)
paintings.story: Madonna and Child is a 1496 oil on panel painting by Cima da Conegliano, now in the Museo Civico in Gemona del Friuli.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child (Cima, Florence)
paintings.story: Madonna and Child is an oil on panel painting by Cima da Conegliano, created c. 1504, that now hangs in the Uffizi in Florence. It has an early copy attributed to Antonio Maria da Carpi, now in the Musei civici di Padova.

paintings.title: Virgin and Child with Saints and Donors
paintings.story: Madonna and Child with Saints is a 1515 oil on panel painting by Cima da Conegliano, now in the Cleveland Museum of Art, Ohio.
facts: At the bottom left and right it portrays the married couple who probably commissioned it for private devotion.
The husband may have been named Antonio, since the saint presenting him is Anthony the Great.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child Enthroned with Two Male Saints
paintings.story: Madonna and Child Enthroned with Two Male Saints is a 1489 oil-on-panel painting by the Italian Renaissance painter Cima da Conegliano, previously owned by the church of San Dionisio in the Zermen district of Feltre and now in the Museo Civico in that town.
facts: The cymatium at the top shows Jesus between Saint Peter and Saint Paul.

The saints in the main panel Denis on the left and a martyr with a palm on the right, but it is not known for certain who the latter is - the museum itself identifies him as Victor, but the Fondazione Federico Zeri catalogue has him as Eleutherius.

paintings.title: Virgin and Child with Saint Andrew and Saint Peter
paintings.story: The Virgin and Child with Saint Andrew and Saint Peter is an unfinished painting by an unknown artist in the studio of Cima da Conegliano. It is believed to have been created in the late 15th or early 16th century. It is now in the National Galleries of Scotland, in Edinburgh.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child with Saint Francis and Saint Clare
paintings.story: Madonna and Child with Saint Francis and Saint Clare is an oil-on-panel painting created ca. 1492–1495 by the Italian Renaissance painter Cima da Conegliano, now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, in New York.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child with Saint John the Baptist and Saint Francis
paintings.story: Madonna and Child with Saint John the Baptist and Saint Francis is a 1489 oil-on-panel painting by the Italian Renaissance artist Cima da Conegliano, now in the Musée du Petit Palais in Avignon.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child with Saint Jerome and Saint John the Baptist
paintings.story: Madonna and Child with Saint Jerome and Saint John the Baptist is an oil-on-panel painting executed ca. 1492–1495 by the Italian Renaissance painter Cima da Conegliano, now in the National Gallery of Art (NGA) in Washington.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child with Saint Jerome and Saint Mary Magdalene
paintings.story: Madonna and Child with Saint Jerome and Saint Mary Magdalene is a 1495 oil-on-panel painting by the Italian Renaissance painter Cima da Conegliano, now in the Alte Pinakothek, Munich, having been bought for the Bavarian royal collections in 1815 from the Empress Josephine's collection at Malmaison.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child with Saints (Cima, Berlin)
paintings.story: Madonna and Child with Saints is an oil on panel painting by Cima da Conegliano, created in 1504, now in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin. From left to right the accompanying saints are Peter, Romuald, Benedict of Nursia and Paul.

paintings.title: Sacred Conversation (Cima, Milan)
paintings.story: The Sacred Conversation or Madonna and Child Enthroned with praying brothers and devotees, Saint Sebastian, Saint John the Baptist, Saint Mary Magdalene and Saint Roch is a 1490 oil-on-panel painting by the Italian artist Cima da Conegliano, now in the Pinacoteca di Brera in Milan.

paintings.title: Saint Lanfranc Enthroned Between Saints John the Baptist and Liberius
paintings.story: Saint Lanfranc Enthroned Between Saints John the Baptist and Liberius is an oil painting by Cima da Conegliano dating to c. 1515–1516. It is now in the Fitzwilliam Museum, Cambridge. It shows Saint Lanfranc on a throne, between John the Baptist and Saint Liberius.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child (Cima, Minneapolis)
paintings.story: Madonna and Child is an oil-on-panel painting created ca. 1500–1504 by the Italian artist Cima da Conegliano, now in the Minneapolis Institute of Arts.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child (Cima, Amsterdam)
paintings.story: Madonna and Child is a 1512–1517 oil on canvas painting by Cima da Conegliano, now in the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child (Cima, Cardiff)
paintings.story: Madonna and Child is an oil-on-panel painting by Cima da Conegliano, created in 1500, now in the National Museum of Wales in Cardiff.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child (Cima, Detroit)
paintings.story: Madonna and Child is a 1499–1502 oil on panel painting by Giovanni Battista Cima (1459-1517), now in the Detroit Institute of Arts, to which it was given in 1889 by James E. Scripps, having been in Scottish and English collections since around 1842.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child (Cima, Este)
paintings.story: Madonna and Child is an oil-on-panel painting created in 1504 by the Italian Renaissance painter Cima da Conegliano, now in the Museo nazionale atestino in Este. It is the most important pictorial work in the museum, which is mainly dedicated to archeology.

paintings.title: Virgin and Child (Cima, London, c. 1496–1499)
paintings.story: The Virgin and Child is a 1496–1499 oil on panel painting by Cima da Conegliano, bought in 1858 by the National Gallery, London, where it still hangs.

paintings.title: Virgin and Child (Cima, London, c. 1499–1502)
paintings.story: The Virgin and Child is a 1499–1502 oil on panel painting by Cima da Conegliano, now in the National Gallery, London, to which it was bequeathed by George Salting in 1910.

paintings.title: Virgin and Child (Cima, London, c. 1505)
paintings.story: The Virgin and Child is a 1505 oil on panel painting by Cima da Conegliano, now in the National Gallery, London, which bought it in 1860.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child in a Landscape (Cima, Los Angeles)
paintings.story: Madonna and Child is a 1496–1499 oil on panel painting by Cima da Conegliano, now in the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.
facts: Unusually for the artist, who usually produced unique works, this one seems to belong to a group of at least five works produced from a single cartoon.

paintings.title: Virgin and Child before a Landscape
paintings.story: Virgin and Child before a Landscape is an undated oil-on-panel painting by the Italian Renaissance artist Cima da Conegliano, now in the Philadelphia Museum of Art, which acquired it as part of the John G. Johnson collection in 1917.

paintings.title: Virgin and Child in a Landscape (Cima, Raleigh)
paintings.story: Virgin and Child in a Landscape is a 1496–1499 oil on panel painting by Cima da Conegliano, now in the North Carolina Museum of Art, in Raleigh.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child Enthroned with Two Virgin Martyrs
paintings.story: Madonna and Child Enthroned with Two Virgin Martyrs is an oil on panel painting by Cima da Conegliano, created in 1495, now in the Memphis Brooks Museum of Art.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child with Saints James the Great and Jerome (Cima)
paintings.story: Madonna and Child Enthroned with Saint James and Saint Jerome is a 1489 oil painting by Cima da Conegliano, originally painted on panel and later transferred to canvas. It shows James the Great and Jerome either side of an enthroned Madonna and Child and now hangs in the Pinacoteca civica in Vicenza, housed in the Palazzo Chiericati.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child with Saints (Cima, Nivå)
paintings.story: Madonna and Child with Saints is an undated oil-on-panel painting by the Italian Renaissance artist Cima da Conegliano, now in the Nivaagaards Malerisamling in Nivå, Denmark. Its dimensions are 71.5 cm x 102.5 cm. Its small size means it was probably a devotional image for a private house.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child with Saints John the Baptist and Catherine of Alexandria (Cima)
paintings.story: Madonna and Child with Saint John the Baptist and Saint Catherine of Alexandria is a 1515 oil on canvas painting by Cima da Conegliano, now in the Morgan Library in New York.

paintings.title: Virgin and Child with Saints (attributed to Cima)
paintings.story: The Virgin and Child with Saints is an oil-on-canvas painting attributed to Cima da Conegliano, created in 1513–1518, now in the National Gallery, London, to which it was bequeathed in 1916.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child with Saints (Fogg Art Museum)
paintings.story: Madonna and Child with Saints is a 1515 oil on canvas painting, now in the Fogg Art Museum in Cambridge (Massachusetts). Previously attributed to Cima da Conegliano, it is now attributed to an artist in the circle of Giovanni Bellini.

paintings.title: Head of a Female Saint
paintings.story: Head of a Female Saint is an undated oil on panel painting by Cima da Conegliano, now in the Museo Poldi Pezzoli in Milan. It depicts an unknown female saint, since there are no visible attributes that can help to her identification.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child with Saint Catherine and Saint Nicholas
paintings.story: Madonna and Child with Saint Catherine and Saint Nicholas is a 1510-1517 oil on canvas painting by Cima da Conegliano, now on long-term loan to the Yale University Art Gallery from the Barker Welfare Foundation in memory of Catherine Barker and Charles V. Hickox.

paintings.title: Mestre Altarpiece
paintings.story: The Mestre Altarpiece was a c. 1500–1502 altarpiece by Cima da Conegliano. The side panels of Saint Roch and Saint Sebastian from the work are now in the Musée des Beaux-Arts in Strasbourg, whilst the central section showing St Catherine of Alexandria and the lunette of Madonna and Child between St Dominic and St Francis are both in the Wallace Collection in London. The central section is signed on a pedestal "JOANIS BABTISTE CONEGLANESIS OPUS".

paintings.title: Baptism of Christ (Cima)
paintings.story: Baptism of Christ is a painting by Italian Renaissance painter Cima da Conegliano, dating from 1492. It is an oil painting on panel and is housed in the church of San Giovanni in Bragora in Venice.
facts: The painting portrays Christ at the center of the scene, standing with joined hands.
His attitude is that of humble submission to baptism, which is being given him by Saint John the Baptist, who appears on the right.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child Enthroned with John the Baptist and Mary Magdalene
paintings.story: Madonna and Child Enthroned with John the Baptist and Mary Magdalene is a 1511–1513 oil on panel painting by Cima da Conegliano. Originally in the monastery church of San Domenico in Parma, it was seized by the French occupiers in 1811 and taken to Paris, remaining there after the Congress of Vienna and still in the collections of the Louvre.

paintings.title: Polyptych of Miglionico
paintings.story: The Polyptych of Miglionico is a large, multicompartment Renaissance-style altarpiece painted in 1499 by Cima da Conegliano and housed in the church of Santa Maria Maggiore in the town of Miglionico, province of Matera, Basilicata, Italy.

paintings.title: Conegliano Altarpiece
paintings.story: The Conegliano Altarpiece or Madonna and Child with Angels and Saints is an oil painting produced in 1492 by Cima da Conegliano as the high altarpiece for the Duomo di Conegliano in his birthplace.
facts: The painting was commissioned in the 1490s by Francesco Codroipo and Giovanni della Pasqualina.
At that time, Cima was active in Venice under the influence of Giovanni Bellini.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child (workshop of Cima, Paris)
paintings.story: Madonna and Child is a 1504–1507 oil on panel painting by Cima da Conegliano, now in the Louvre, in Paris.

paintings.title: Olera Altarpiece
paintings.story: Olera Altarpiece is an oil on panel nine-panel altarpiece by Cima da Conegliano, created c. 1486–1488, housed in the parish church in Olera.

paintings.title: Madonna and Child (Cima, private collection)
paintings.story: Madonna and Child is a 1504 oil on panel painting by Cima da Conegliano, now in a private collection. It was last sold at Christie's in London on 25 November 1966 as part of a sale of works from Sir Herbert Cook's collection and is therefore sometimes known as the Cook Madonna, not to be confused with another painting of that name by Crivelli now known to be the central panel of the Porto San Giorgio Altarpiece.

paintings.title: Virgin and Child with Saint Paul and Saint Francis
paintings.story: The Virgin and Child with Saint Paul and Saint Francis is a 1508-1530 oil on poplar panel. It was previously attributed to Cima da Conegliano but now thought to be by one of his studio assistants, possibly using workshop drawings by the artist himself, since all four figures appear in autograph works by the painter. It is now in the National Gallery, London.

paintings.title: Madonna and child between Saint George and Saint James
Giudizio di Mida, Cima da Conegliano
Christ on the Cross with the Virgin and Saint John the Evangelist
paintings.story: Alternative Title: The Crucifixion Description: The Virgin and Saint John mourn at the foot of a tall cross set in a bleak landscape with a darkening sky. To the right, Christ prays in the Garden of Gethsemane whilst his disciples sleep - the Agony in the Garden. To the left are three scenes from Christ's Passion set within, or in front of, Pontius Pilate's palace. The denial of Saint Peter is at the bottom; Pilate Washing his Hands is above, alongside the Crowning with Thorns. The smaller scenes may have been painted by an assistant, but the landscape in particular shows Cima's knowledge of developments in Venetian painting.
